abstract: Long COVID is associated with persistent immune dysregulation, but whether immunity to latent viruses is also altered remains unclear. We profiled herpesvirus-specific antibodies and T-cell responses in people with long COVID and recovered convalescent controls at 4, 8, and 24 months after SAR-CoV-2 infection. Overall antibody reactivity and abundance against cytomegalovirus (CMV) and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) responder frequencies and circulating B-cell subsets were broadly preserved, but early antibody avidity and virus-specific CD4 T cell response magnitude were reduced. Neither virus nucleic acid was detected in plasma or stool at 4 or 8 months. Here, we show that long COVID is associated with selective, time-dependent alteration of herpesvirus-specific immune memory, including relatively preserved or enhanced CD8 responses and greater representation of selected herpesvirus-associated T-cell receptor clonotypes. Together, these findings indicate altered herpesvirus-specific antibody quality despite broadly preserved antibody abundance. Lower EBV avidity was associated with poorer quality of life and unrecovered status.
hook: People with long COVID show weaker early antibody binding and CD4 T cell responses to CMV and EBV
summary: Blood from people with long COVID and recovered controls was profiled at 4, 8, and 24 months after infection. Antibody amounts were similar, but early antibody avidity and CD4 T cell response were lower, and lower EBV avidity tracked with poorer quality of life. This is an association in a modest cohort and does not show that altered herpesvirus immunity causes long COVID.
title: Altered herpesvirus-specific immune response is associated with long COVID
